slides.title: Even the Prophet didn't control hearts
slides.promise: What we have actually been asked to do, from The Mirror.

slides.head: When you speak about faith
slides.body: A quiet correction for anyone who speaks to others about faith. The task is real, but it stops where another person's heart begins.

slides.head: The Messenger's duty
slides.body: A verse of Surah al-Ra‘d (13:40) describes it as delivering the message, and leaves the account of each person to God.

slides.head: What he was not asked to do
slides.body: He was not required to force the message into people's hearts, to search their souls, or to pronounce their final judgement.

slides.quote: So remind them; you are only one who reminds. You are not appointed to control them.

slides.head: What it means to remind
slides.body: A person who reminds points towards the truth, but does not force anyone towards it.

slides.head: The mind and the heart
slides.body: He speaks to the mind and to the heart, and makes no attempt to take control of either.

slides.head: The question for us
slides.body: If the Prophet was not appointed to control people's faith, how can anyone after him claim authority over their consciences?

slides.head: Convey, not judge
items: Leave each person's account to God.
Speak to the mind and the heart.

slides.head: Read more in The Mirror
slides.ask: Send this to someone who talks to others about faith.
